title: kbjob.py serve stops with a refusal when a running job was cancelled meanwhile, since run_job's final move finds a terminal job
goal: kj_exec.run_job, when its job was moved to cancelled while the child ran (kbjob.py cancel), leaves the job cancelled, prints one line saying so and returns cancelled, so kbjob.py serve goes on with the next queued job instead of ending with exit 2

run: import sys,os,tempfile,time,subprocess,threading,io; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); from argparse import Namespace; from pathlib import Path; import coord,kj_store,kj_exec; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); s=os.path.join(d,"c.sqlite"); j=kj_store.submit(".","check","",None,{"name":"backlog-check"},store=s)["job"]; mv=lambda to: coord.job_transition(Namespace(key="job/"+j,to=to,field=[],store=s),time.time); mv("running"); log=Path(d)/"output.log"; log.write_bytes(b""); kj_exec.start_child=lambda r,c,p: (subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,"-c","import time; time.sleep(1)"]),0); threading.Timer(0.3,lambda: mv("cancelled")).start(); kj_exec.run_job(s,j,kj_store.read_record(s,j),".",log,"t",io.StringIO())
